Definition: of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron:--towel.
BiblicalUsage: léntion means a linen towel, and once is enough to see what it is doing. In John 13:4, "and took a towel"; and in John 13:5, "and to wipe [them] with the towel wherewith he was girded.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the towel is the whole gospel in one gesture — the Lord laid aside His garments, girded Himself, and washed feet.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
